_meta.indication: CARDAMYST is a calcium channel blocker indicated for the conversion of acute symptomatic episodes of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT) to sinus rhythm in adults.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter, event-driven trial; patients randomized 1:1 to self-administer CARDAMYST 70 mg or placebo nasal spray at home for a perceived PSVT episode, with an optional repeat 70 mg dose after 10 minutes if the arrhythmia persisted.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult patients with a history of symptomatic paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT); primary efficacy population of 184 subjects with adjudication-confirmed PSVT episodes.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Adjudicated termination of a confirmed episode of PSVT and conversion to sinus rhythm (SR) for at least 30 seconds within 30 minutes of the start of study drug.
pivotal_trials.n: 692 patients randomized 1:1; 255 self-administered study drug, of which 184 episodes were adjudication-confirmed PSVT (primary efficacy population).
pivotal_trials.result: Kaplan-Meier estimates of conversion to sinus rhythm within 30 minutes were 64.3% for etripamil versus 31.2% for placebo; hazard ratio 2.62 (95% CI 1.66, 4.15), p<0.001. Median time-to-conversion was 17.2 minutes with CARDAMYST versus 53.5 minutes with placebo.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence >5%) are local administration-site reactions: nasal discomfort (28% for 70 mg vs 6% placebo), nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, throat irritation, and epistaxis. No SAEs or deaths occurred within 24 hours of etripamil dosing. Serious potential risk is dizziness/syncope due to hypotension and/or bradyarrhythmias/AV block; 0.4% experienced clinically significant hypotension during test dose.
target_moa: Etripamil is an intranasally administered non-dihydropyridine L-type calcium channel blocker (a verapamil analog) that targets AV-nodal tissue to slow AV-node conduction and restore sinus rhythm.
modality: Small molecule (calcium channel blocker; verapamil analog nasal spray)

boxed_warning.content: No boxed warning; the finalized Prescribing Information BOXED WARNING section is marked N/A.

summary.text: Standard-review NDA for etripamil nasal spray. The original NDA (received 3/27/2024) received a Complete Response letter on March 27, 2025, for product-quality/nitrosamine deficiencies and an incomplete facility inspection. The applicant held a Type A meeting on June 4, 2025, and resubmitted a class 2 resubmission on June 13, 2025 (PDUFA goal December 13, 2025), addressing the OPQ deficiencies; with no new deficiencies, the application was approved. No accelerated approval, breakthrough, fast track, orphan, or priority-review designations were applied.

The Applicant had Type A Meeting on June 4, 2025, to discuss issues identified in the March 27, 2025, complete response letter. The Applicant resubmitted their NDA on June 13, 2025.

On June 13, 2025, the Applicant resubmitted NDA 218571. On July 3, 2025, this resubmission was acknowledged as a complete, class 2 resubmission, with the Prescription Drug User Fee Act goal date of December 13, 2025.

The resubmission did not include any new clinical-pharmacology, clinical, or device-related data. OPQ review dated October 23, 2025, recommended approval. Pharmacology-toxicology review discipline also recommended approval. No new deficiencies were identified. Hence, for NDA 218571, the regulatory action for current review cycle is approval.
